meta.audience: Small business owners / solopreneurs (primary, $99-297) + working professionals (secondary, $47-97)

weight_definitions.demand: Volume and growth rate of people actively seeking this skill
weight_definitions.wtp: Willingness to pay - price tolerance and budget authority of the buyer
weight_definitions.gap: Inverse of saturation - how underserved the need is relative to demand
weight_definitions.build: Feasibility of shipping a quality 1-hour MVP in under 4 weeks, including durability against tool churn

meta.methodology_note: Rev C: card language simplified and competitors described by category rather than name; source links still point to the original pages so every claim stays checkable. Each topic now carries a target learner profile and three scaffolded objectives, written to Bloom's revised taxonomy with an observable verb and a stated criterion. Source tiers: [A] primary, [B] secondary, [C] weak.

topics.title: AI Policy in an Afternoon: Governance for Businesses Without a Legal Team
topics.one_liner: A working AI usage policy plus staff literacy briefing, sized for a company of 5-50 people.
evidence: EU AI Act enforcement of the AI literacy rules begins 2 August 2026 [B]
Article 4 has required AI literacy for all staff since February 2025 [B]
Small firms lack the resources to manage AI risk in a structured way, while large firms build dedicated governance teams [B]
Regulators are expected to treat missing AI training as an aggravating factor in wider enforcement [B]
Responsible AI ranks #6 and Information Privacy #9 among the fastest-growing skills [A]
Compliance purchases carry the highest price tolerance of any category [C]
topics.why_underserved: Material on the AI Act is written by law firms for enterprise counsel. Nothing is sized for a 12-person company that needs one policy document and a short staff briefing.
topics.risks: MATERIAL. In May 2026 EU lawmakers provisionally agreed to shift the Article 4 obligation from individual organizations to member states. If that is finalized, this becomes a best-practice sale rather than a compliance sale. Check the current status before building. Also EU-anchored: US-only buyers need a different hook, such as client contract terms or procurement questionnaires.
topics.buildability_notes: Template-driven. A policy document, a short briefing deck, and a self-assessment checklist. Low production cost, high perceived value.
topics.learner_profile: Owner or operations lead at a 5-50 person company that already uses AI tools informally. No legal team, no compliance officer, no budget for outside counsel.

objectives.statement: Classify ten common AI uses in small firms as low, limited, or high risk, matching the reference key on at least eight of the ten.
Audit your own team's AI use and produce an inventory naming every tool, task, and data type in play, with at least five entries.
Draft a one-page AI use policy that includes all four required elements: permitted uses, prohibited data, disclosure rules, and a review date.

topics.title: The Third Week: Making AI Stick After the Novelty Wears Off
topics.one_liner: The only offering on the market aimed at the middle of adoption rather than the beginning.
evidence: Across every provider examined, four things are missing: measuring time saved, recovering from a failed attempt, sustaining use, and handing a workflow to someone else [A]
Learner reviews complain about implementation, not information — one describes a course as an 'AI pep rally' with no demonstration of how to actually do the thing [B]
People stop using AI tools because the tool 'feels like managing another job' [C]
Only 8% of businesses reach advanced adoption; most stall at the experimental stage [C]
topics.why_underserved: The market has solved inspiration and getting started. Nobody teaches what happens in week three. Every syllabus examined ends at the first successful output.
topics.risks: MATERIAL. This may be underserved because it is hard to sell. Nobody searches for 'AI adoption durability' — there is no keyword, no job title, no certificate. It has to be sold on the symptom ('you tried it and stopped'), not the category. That also means search volume cannot validate it. Only a landing page with a real price will.
topics.buildability_notes: 12 lessons, 5-8 minutes each, about 75 minutes total. No tool dependency and no screen recordings that expire, so it will not need re-recording when the next model ships.
topics.learner_profile: Owner or solo operator who already tried AI, got real value for a week or two, and quietly stopped. Not a beginner. Not looking for another tool.

objectives.statement: Apply the time-audit method to one recurring task and calculate hours saved per month, recording both a before and an after figure.
Diagnose which of three failure patterns — novelty decay, quality drift, or context loss — stopped that workflow, citing at least two pieces of evidence.
Evaluate the workflow against the keep, repair, or retire decision rule, and justify your verdict using the measured time saving and your stated quality floor.

topics.title: Don't Ship It Blind: Verifying AI Output Before It Reaches a Client
topics.one_liner: A repeatable verification routine for anyone whose name goes on AI-assisted work.
evidence: Critical Thinking enrollments grew 185% among learners focused on generative AI [A]
Research finds that the more people trust an AI tool, the less they scrutinize what it returns [B]
Researchers call the pattern 'cognitive surrender' — accepting AI output with little review [B]
43% of workers worry that using AI could make their job obsolete; verification is the counter-position [C]
Across the market, coverage of this topic amounts to roughly one short video [A]
topics.why_underserved: Writing on this is plentiful but almost entirely academic or opinion. Very little of it gives someone a checklist they can actually run in five minutes.
topics.risks: Soft-skill topics convert worse than tool topics in consumer markets. Sell the consequence — client and reputational risk — not the virtue. Strongest as a B2B or professional-services offer.
topics.buildability_notes: Content plus graded exercises. No tooling, no vendor dependency, almost no obsolescence risk. The best long-tail asset on this list.

sources.label: Forbes: AI is eroding critical thinking at work
APA Monitor: how AI is reshaping human skills

topics.learner_profile: Consultant, freelancer, or professional-services staffer whose name goes on AI-assisted work before a client sees it.

objectives.statement: Describe all three ways AI output fails — fabrication, plausible but wrong reasoning, and silent omission — and supply one example of each from your own field, for three examples in total.
Apply the five-minute verification checklist to a sample deliverable and flag at least four of the five planted errors.
Evaluate a client-bound deliverable against a quality floor you define in advance, and justify your ship or revise decision in writing.

topics.title: Automate One Real Process in 60 Minutes
topics.one_liner: Build a single working AI-assisted automation end to end, using the learner's own recurring task.
evidence: The automation-plus-AI skill combination is the most requested on job boards and freelance marketplaces [C]
Demand for automation specialists is outpacing the supply of trained people [C]
79% of organizations already run AI agents in production [C]
Workflow automation returns an average of 171%; 62% of companies report returns above 100% [C]
AI integration grew 178% year over year, the second-fastest skill measured [A]
topics.why_underserved: Automation courses exist in quantity, but they teach the platform rather than the business outcome, and assume a technical user. The version framed around one process and measurable hours saved is thinner ground.
topics.risks: Highest tool-churn exposure on this list. Every major automation platform shipped significant AI changes in the last cycle, so screen recordings will date fast. Script around the pattern, not the button positions.
topics.buildability_notes: Needs screen recording and a working reference build — the heaviest production lift here. Strongest ROI story and the easiest to price.

sources.label: Digital Applied - Make vs Zapier vs n8n 2026

topics.learner_profile: Owner or operations lead with at least one recurring task that eats hours every week. Comfortable with software, not a developer.

objectives.statement: Apply all three selection criteria — frequency, time cost, and rule clarity — to your weekly task list, and select one automation candidate with a one-sentence justification.
Break the chosen task into a written workflow spec of at least three steps, separating each trigger, action, and check.
Build and run the automation end to end, producing a workflow that completes the task correctly on three consecutive live runs.

topics.title: Your First AI-Generated Marketing Video, Start to Publish
topics.one_liner: One finished, on-brand short video produced inside the session.
evidence: AI video generation and editing grew 329% year over year, the fastest-growing skill measured [A]
The AI video market is growing at 36.2% a year [B]
Content creation is the fastest-growing skill among learners focused on generative AI [A]
Production costs fell roughly 97% since 2020 — work that cost $1,500 now renders for under $15 [B]
Demand concentrates in marketing, education, and social media [B]
topics.why_underserved: It is not, particularly. Demand is large but so is supply, and commercial offerings are crowded. Included because raw demand and a clear income path partly offset the saturation.
topics.risks: The most crowded topic here and the fastest to decay — tools turn over in months. Differentiate by industry rather than teaching 'AI video' in general, or drop it in favor of a higher-gap topic.
topics.buildability_notes: Needs produced video assets and tool walkthroughs. Highest production cost and shortest shelf life. Budget a refresh every cycle.

sources.label: Grand View Research - AI video generator market

topics.learner_profile: Owner or marketer who needs regular short-form video and currently either outsources it or skips it.

objectives.statement: Identify all four elements of a short-form video brief — audience, single message, call to action, and format specification — and record each one for your own planned video.
Apply your brief to generate draft footage and voice, selecting at least three usable candidate clips.
Produce one publish-ready video that meets every item on the brand checklist — aspect ratio, captions, and call to action — and export it.

topics.title: Find Your AI Use Case (SMB-scaled)
topics.one_liner: Teaches owners how to identify where AI actually fits in their specific business, before they buy a single tool.
evidence: 77% of small business non-adopters say they see no use case that applies to them [C]
62% cite lack of understanding; 60% have no in-house expertise [C]
47% of those already using AI still find tool selection difficult [C]
Practical training is the top support need small business owners name [C]
topics.why_underserved: REVISED DOWN in rev B. A large enterprise vendor already offers a free four-hour course covering substantially this ground, with 8,319 enrollments and a 4.7 rating. The remaining gap is narrow: that course is tied to the vendor's own platform, expects two prior courses, and is written for executives at large organizations. An independent version sized for small business is differentiated, but no longer open ground. [A]
topics.risks: Competes directly with a free, well-rated incumbent. Differentiation rests only on audience size and vendor neutrality, which is a thin moat.
topics.buildability_notes: No software dependency — a framework plus a scoring worksheet. Ages well and will not break when a vendor changes its interface. Fastest here to produce.
topics.learner_profile: Owner of a small business who has heard AI matters but cannot see where it fits in their specific operation.

objectives.statement: Describe all four task characteristics that predict AI suitability — repetition, text density, tolerance for review, and clear success criteria — and state each in your own words.
Apply those four characteristics to score at least eight tasks from your own operation using the supplied worksheet.
Analyze the scored list to rank your top three candidates, explaining why each outranks the alternatives.
